items.definition:
the process of making something free from bacteria or germs
Sterilization of medical instruments is crucial for patient safety.

shareholder
The company's stockholders will vote on the new proposal.

a Polynesian carving or style
The restaurant had a strong tiki theme with carved statues.

a small cluster of soft, fluffy strands
A small tuft of grass grew between the cracks in the pavement.

a small glass bottle
The vaccine was stored in a small glass vial.

financial support paid to a former spouse after divorce
He was ordered to pay alimony to his ex-wife.

anxiety or fear that something bad or unpleasant will happen; understanding
He felt a sense of apprehension before the exam.

a person who attacks another
The victim was unable to identify her assailant.

an improvised barrier erected across a street or other thoroughfare to prevent the passage of persons or vehicles
The police set up a barricade to block the road.

a person who writes a biography
The biographer spent years researching the subject's life.

the state or quality of being black
The blackness of the night made it hard to see anything.

an isolated hill or mountain with steep sides and a flat top
The lone butte stood prominently on the desert horizon.

the quality of being logical and consistent
The essay lacked coherence and was difficult to follow.

the execution of a person by nailing or binding them to a cross
The crucifixion of Jesus is a central event in Christianity.

a dome-shaped muscular partition separating the thorax from the abdomen
The diaphragm plays a crucial role in breathing.

a place where medicines are prepared and dispensed
He went to the dispensary to pick up his prescription.

the act of officially joining a course, school, or organization
University enrolment numbers have increased this year.

a person who carries out a death sentence
The executioner wore a black hood.

a slender threadlike object or fiber
The light bulb's filament glowed brightly.

a painting done rapidly in watercolor on wet plaster on a wall or ceiling
The chapel ceiling was adorned with a beautiful fresco.

a warship with a mixed armament, generally smaller than a destroyer
The frigate sailed across the ocean.

the main body of an aircraft
The fuselage of the plane was made of lightweight materials.

a person's or animal's manner of walking
The horse had a peculiar gait.

gold leaf or paint applied to a surface
The old frame was covered in faded gilt.

a person who goes to a specified place or event
She's a regular concert-goer.

dirt, especially soot, coal dust, or a greasy film
The old windows were covered in years of grime.

an inhabitant of a highland region, especially the Scottish Highlands
The Highlander wore a traditional kilt.

the action of admitting someone to a hospital
His hospitalization was due to a severe infection.

A display showing the names and scores of the leading competitors.
Her name was at the top of the leaderboard.

A heavy or awkward thing to carry; a projection.
The old suitcase was a real lug to carry up the stairs.

The amount added to the cost price to determine the selling price; a set of instructions for formatting text.
The store applies a 30% markup on all its products.

A television drama or documentary series with a limited number of episodes.
The historical miniseries was very popular.

The process of managing something badly or inefficiently.
The company's financial problems were due to mismanagement.

egg of a louse
The comb helped remove nits from her hair.

a person rejected by society
He felt like an outcast after moving to a new school.

a point on a ranking scale
His test score was in the 90th percentile.

a chief magistrate or a senior student
She was appointed school prefect in her final year.

a decisive defeat
The team suffered a humiliating rout in the final game.

a type of bacteria that causes food poisoning
The restaurant was shut down due to a salmonella outbreak.

a sharp object used as a knife, especially one improvised in prison
He fashioned a shiv out of a toothbrush.

the state of being a famous performer
Her talent quickly led her to stardom.

a flash of lightning accompanied by thunder; a sudden, shocking event
A thunderbolt struck the old oak tree.

a switch or button that can be set to two positions
Press the toggle to turn the feature on or off.

a natural object or animal believed by a particular society to have spiritual significance and adopted by it as an emblem
The tribe carved a tall totem pole.

(informal) a tournament
They are preparing for the big chess tourney next month.

an open sore on an external or internal surface of the body
The doctor diagnosed him with a stomach ulcer.

the degree of skill with which a product is made or a job done
The antique clock showed excellent workmanship.

a small brown bird
A tiny wren built its nest in the rose bush.

the flow of air
The airflow in the room was poor.

a swift-running deer-like ruminant
The antelope grazed peacefully on the savanna.

a horizontal bar used by ballet dancers for support
The dancers held onto the barre during their warm-up exercises.

a device that produces a powerful blast; a fictional energy weapon
The hero fired his blaster at the alien.

a large cave or a chamber in a cave
The explorers ventured deep into the dark cavern.

the qualities of a knight, such as courage, honor, and courtesy
His act of opening the door for her was a small gesture of chivalry.

a defensive player in American football
The cornerback intercepted the pass and ran it back for a touchdown.

a situation where people are caught between opposing forces
Civilians were caught in the crossfire during the battle.

a person or entity that owes money
The debtor struggled to repay the loan.

a person who sends out vehicles or messages
The police dispatcher sent officers to the scene of the accident.

a current of air; a serving of beer from a barrel
There's a cold draught coming from under the door.

a person who abandons a course of study or a competition
He became a successful entrepreneur despite being a college dropout.

a person who is concerned with protecting the natural environment
She became an environmentalist after seeing the effects of pollution.

the process of turning from liquid into vapor
The evaporation of water from the lake increased during the summer.

the triangular upper part of a wall at the end of a ridged roof
The house had a distinctive gable roof.

a type of thick woollen sweater; a breed of dairy cattle
He wore a warm guernsey on the cold day.
